content:
deploy-bot: 🚀 starting canary rollout release/serve-v3 -> canary=10% on pool=canary-us-west-2

maya (oncall): seeing healthcheck failures on canary nodes, +5xx spike on /v1/generate :rotating_light:

alex (sre): paging — I'll take it. what's the canary config? any new feature flags?

sam (eng-runtime): we flipped `new-conn-pool` for the canary only, plus a smaller kernel change. readiness probe failing with `ERROR: kv-cache init timeout` in logs.

maya (oncall): incident-bot paging (high 5xx for canary) — customers might hit it if traffic routed.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-77 - Canary 5xx / healthcheck failures. Severity: P2. Assigned: alex (sre).

alex (sre): quick check — canary nodes showing 38% 5xx, steady for ~2m. backend errors `503` with trace id examples: `trace=5a7c...`

sam (eng-runtime): past hour baseline is <0.1% 5xx. This is abnormal regression. Repro locally by enabling `new-conn-pool` for a few requests.

jordan (support): any known customer-facing errors yet? seeing a tiny uptick of error reports from a single enterprise tenant on EU region but most traffic unaffected.

alex (sre): mitigation plan: 1) pause routing to canary, 2) flip feature flag kill-switch for `new-conn-pool`, 3) revert canary deployment if health doesn't recover. Executing step 1 now.

deploy-bot: routing paused -> canary=0%.

maya (oncall): confirm kill-switch location? is it feature-flag service or runtime flag?

sam (eng-runtime): it's a LaunchDarkly flag `new-conn-pool` set in rollout group `canary-serve-v3`. I'll flip it now to `off` globally for canary group.

sam (eng-runtime): flipped `new-conn-pool` -> off for canary group.

alex (sre): health checks improving? current 5xx rate down to 12% within 90s. still elevated.

maya (oncall): pushing for rollback?

alex (sre): starting canary rollback to previous replicaset. deploy-bot, please initiate rollback job `release/serve-v3@prev`.

deploy-bot: rollback started -> job id rb-2026-0315-9. Estimated time ~3m.

sam (eng-runtime): grabbing logs from canary nodes before they terminate: attached snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T10:14:12Z] runtime: failed healthcheck: timeout waiting for kv-cache
[2026-03-15T10:14:13Z] http: response 503 for /v1/generate trace=5a7c... instance=canary-03
[2026-03-15T10:14:14Z] connpool: init latency spike 1800ms
```

alex (sre): rb job completed, new pods are old-replicaset. Canaries terminated. Health metrics returning to baseline.

incident-bot: update: INC-2026-0315-77 status -> mitigated (canary rollback + feature flag off).

jordan (support): notifying affected tenant rep, advising retry and that we rolled back. Any guidance for customers who saw errors?

maya (oncall): prepare postmortem checklist: timeline, root cause hypothesis (`conn pool init race under new kernel path` + flag interactions), impact scope, revert steps, tests to add.

alex (sre): quick impact estimate: canary served ~0.8% of total traffic while enabled. Observed 5xx concentrated to canary instances and one EU tenant reported errors — unlikely to be broad customer impact.

sam (eng-runtime): next steps for dev: add stricter readiness gating around kv-cache init, integration test for `new-conn-pool` under slow disk/hotstart, and a safer rollout (gradual ramp + synthetic checks).

maya (oncall): I'll hand off to next oncall in 30m. alex, please add any followups to the incident ticket. jordan, send a short note to support with incident summary.

alex (sre): will add RCA draft and assign owners. thanks all for fast response. :thumbsup:

jordan (support): sent tenant note: "We've reverted a canary change that caused transient 503s; please retry. Reach out if you still see issues."

maya (oncall): handing off: oncall-next is @lina. Lina — all clear now, rb done, flag off, incident mitigated. Full RCA in ticket INC-2026-0315-77.

lina (oncall): thanks, picked up. Will review ticket and follow up in morning.

alex (sre): final note for logbook: root cause likely mis-ordered init in conn pool + insufficient canary gating. Recovery: kill-switch + rollback at 10:17 UTC. No broad customer outage.

incident-bot: INC-2026-0315-77 closed as mitigated.
